parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a nationally imposed, universal-exposure document/entry screen with locally protective law. Every trans visitor faces the national sex-marker regime at passport/visa stage: mismatch or 'reasonable doubt' triggers refusal, case-note tagging, and potential lifetime fraud ineligibility; foreign governments have issued advisories after documented detentions. If detention occurs, national custody conditions are documented as abusive. But within this division the visitor meets working anti-discrimination law, hate-crime coverage, panic-defence abolition, and a documented court remedy; adult care access is not restricted, and no local facility ban is documented here. Minor travellers face care bans and school/sports exclusion. Severity is mostly refusal, delay and humiliation rather than imprisonment; state protections are real and operative. Net: Elevated-to-Reduced boundary, 0.60.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented universal exposure: passports/visas must reflect sex assigned at birth; officers must refuse cases with 'reasonable doubt' on sex; potential permanent fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report confiscation/stranding; allied states issued advisories after detentions of foreign citizens.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties litigation ongoing; X passports issued before Feb 2025 remain valid; legal-aid FAQ exists; fraud finding requires four elements and waiver exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud referral can escalate into immigration detention, where documented abuse awaits; national screening overrides this division's protective identity-document rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national custody harms: corrections bureau policies described as conversion therapy, hormone denial; immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men; reporting on trans prisoners ceased.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders enjoined in court; habeas and consular access presumably available but not documented for trans visitors specifically.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visa discrepancy or fraud suspicion is the pathway from ordinary travel into this custody system; the interaction, not the base rate, drives severity.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National facilities (including prisons) exclude trans people from congruent facilities; facility bans exist in many other state/provinces, including 4 with criminal exposure; one documented arrest of a trans woman in a women's restroom elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division documents no facility ban in the mapped categories; national funding rules, not state law, govern federal buildings here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Traveller moving between divisions crosses regimes; national facilities override state protections.

care_services.exposure: Adult visitors' care access not restricted here; minors face documented bans on puberty blockers, hormones and surgery from 2026, with provider discipline and private suits; proposed national insurance bars for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed nationally for minor patient records.
care_services.protection: Division anti-discrimination law covers health care; public-insurance surgery ban was lifted in 2017; adult prescriptions unrestricted by documented state rules.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care becomes a legal exposure for providers and potentially the accompanying adult; national subpoena practice raises disclosure risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented national threat-framing: 'gender ideology' removals, counterterrorism strategy targeting 'radically pro-transgender' groups, enforcement orders against schools facilitating transition, anti-trans athlete and passport directives.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment-discrimination ruling and hate-crime statute remain; several hostile orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile national framing raises discovery stakes at every federal touchpoint (border, police checks), amplifying the exposure created by the entry regime.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor travellers face the division's care bans, school sports exclusion (stayed, unresolved), national school-investigation orders, and records subpoenas; guardian exposure if supporting a minor's identity.
minors_guardians.protection: Division anti-bullying and school anti-discrimination protections; highest court ruled to protect trans students' privacy/autonomy (2024); care-ban enforcement status uncertain.
minors_guardians.interaction: Teacher-facilitation prosecution orders make any adult visibly supporting a trans minor a national-law exposure; state protections may not pre-empt federal investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025, second-highest raw count nationally (no denominator); documented assault of a trans woman; elsewhere a documented bathroom-law arrest with 24-hour men's-ward detention.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime enhancements operative; panic defence abolished; county court found a civil-rights violation for striking a trans woman in 2026 — enforcement demonstrated working; 88% public support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response in this division treats anti-trans assault as actionable; no documented local police profiling of trans visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Entry-screening discretion, unpublished case-note practice, and unresolved litigation leave exposure timing unpredictable; sports-ban status and care-ban enforcement status unestablished.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working division civil-rights enforcement, legal-aid resources, and court blocks on several national orders; national equality and document maps let travellers plan.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate at the division level, but the harshest operative rules (entry screening, custody) are national, where remedies are litigation-dependent and unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Border screening friction is comparable — discretionary secondary scrutiny, denial, humiliation without typical criminal escalation — but this dossier adds documented detentions of foreign citizens, a lifetime fraud-bar threat, and documented abusive custody behind that screen, making it materially harsher than 0.55-B.

Similar structure: brief, humiliating official encounters with functioning remedies (the division's court finding against an assailant mirrors 0.65-A's accountability-board outcome). But the national document regime is a universal-exposure measure with refusal and fraud consequences, so this sits at or slightly below 0.65-A.

0.75-C has brief detention, counsel access, compensation for unlawful holding, and no hostile national framing. This dossier lacks documented compensation remedies at the national level, documents abusive custody and state threat-framing, and restricts minor care, so it rates clearly below 0.75-C.

0.35-B features systematic targeted police checks and fines for trans visitors. Here no documented routine police targeting of visitors exists in this division, and state enforcement protects rather than harasses; well above 0.35-B despite the national screen.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime splits by journey stage. Every trans visitor crosses a national entry system that mandates birth-sex markers, directs officers to refuse doubtful cases, and threatens a permanent fraud bar — a universal, unavoidable exposure whose escalation path leads into custody the dossier documents as abusive. That national layer, plus counterterrorism-style threat framing and minor-care bans with school-investigation orders, is the dominant risk mass. Within this division, however, the traveller encounters protective, demonstrably enforced law: anti-discrimination coverage across services and care, hate-crime enhancements, an abolished panic defence, a court enforcing those rights in 2026, and broad public support. Adult visitors face mostly refusal, delay and humiliation rather than imprisonment; travelling minors and their guardians face documented care and school exposures. The combination sits just below the Reduced-Risk band: 0.60.
